origin.description: Add a number of days to an origin. A missing origin is 1970-01-01.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A numeric vector of days to add.

arguments.name: origin
arguments.text: A Date, or something as.Date can coerce. Missing means 1970-01-01. The character string 0000-00-00 means the day before 0000-01-01.

origin.details: The result is as.Date(origin, ...) + x. The special origin "0000-00-00" is as.Date("0000-01-01") - 1, which prints as -1-12-31. Other origins are parsed first, so format applies to the origin string.
origin.example:
x <- as.Date.numeric(c(0, 1, -1), origin = "2000-01-01")
cat(paste(as.character(x), collapse = " "), "\n", sep = "")

translation.description: Add a number of days to an origin. A missing origin is 1970-01-01.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: Days to add. None is an R NA.

arguments.name: origin
arguments.text: A date string or a day count. "0000-00-00" is the day before year 0 January 1, day -719529.

arguments.name: fmt
arguments.text: Format used to parse a character origin. %d/%m/%Y is accepted.

translation.details: Days are proleptic Gregorian. Year 0 is a leap year. R's NA payload is preserved when it is added; a plain NaN stays a plain NaN. Printing truncates the day toward zero, and years are not padded to four digits.
translation.example:
from zoo.as_date import as_date_numeric, format_dates
print(" ".join(format_dates(as_date_numeric([0, 1, -1], origin="2000-01-01"))))
